visual_text: BPPV: brief spinning set off by head position
Dizzy on rolling over? Ask what sets it off.
1 Sit on the couch, head turned 45 degrees
2 Lie back, neck extended 20 degrees, affected ear down
3 Look for brief spinning and eye movements
Dix-Hallpike test as defined in the AAO-HNS guideline, 2017
Alasdair MacLullich
Teaching round
Complete resolution of vertigo in BPPV of the posterior canal
In trials in adults aged 18 to 90, the Epley manoeuvre cleared vertigo more often
Epley manoeuvre: 56 in 100
Sham manoeuvre or control: 21 in 100
5 trials, 273 people, mostly small, short follow-up. BPPV came back in about 36 in 100 after treatment.
Hilton and Pinder, Cochrane 2014
Alasdair MacLullich
Teaching round
Older person with dizziness
Before you reach for a tablet
Ask what sets the dizziness off
Examine for BPPV with the Dix-Hallpike test
Treat, or refer for treatment, with a repositioning manoeuvre
Avoid routine antihistamines or benzodiazepines
Check mobility, balance and falls risk
If neck extension is hard, a side-lying test was used in a study of 75-year-olds. Its accuracy against Dix-Hallpike is not established.
AAO-HNS guideline 2017; Kollen et al. 2012
Alasdair MacLullich
Teaching round
alt_text: Three drawn steps of the Dix-Hallpike test: head turned 45 degrees, lying back with the neck extended 20 degrees, then looking for brief spinning and eye movements.

Bar chart from a Cochrane review of 5 trials, 273 people: complete resolution of vertigo in 56 in 100 after the Epley manoeuvre against 21 in 100 after sham or control. BPPV came back in about 36 in 100.

Checklist for older people with dizziness: ask what sets it off, examine with Dix-Hallpike, treat with a repositioning manoeuvre, avoid routine antihistamines or benzodiazepines, check falls risk. A note says side-lying test accuracy is not established.
